bundle.produced_by: controller agent (Claude) from epistemic-field/1 blindspots, docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md and docs/CLAIMS.md
bundle.notes: Controller seed plus a small set of primary method papers. Literature links establish candidate plausibility only; they do not promote a marker into the QC decision path.

markers.name: Sub-floor fines size distribution
markers.observable: The number and size distribution of fine high-Z objects below the present detection floor.
markers.scientific_question: Is M2060's excess a true fine-particle population or an artefact of scale truncation?
markers.proposition: Resolves the excess fine high-Z population of M2060 below the current detection floor, where it is now cut off by the pixel size.
markers.scientific_definition: Number-size distribution of high-Z (BSE-bright) objects per unit area, extended below the current detection floor and compared with selected-reference micrographs imaged at the same pixel size.
markers.measurement_definition: Equivalent-diameter histogram of high-Z objects from BSE at a finer pixel (low kV), same segmentation rule as the engine; densities per 1000 µm² in bins below and above the current floor; selected-reference micrographs imaged at the same settings.
markers.capture_requirements: Higher-magnification, low-kV BSE on M2060 and on selected-reference micrographs. No new instrument capability: the same acquisition as the controller's ZOOM action.

existing_data_test.note: Cannot be computed from the existing micrographs: the population is truncated at the detection floor.

markers.why_relevant: The REJECT rests on M2060, and its excess objects pile up at the detection floor: the decision-driving population is only partly observed.

known_confounds.label: sub-surface objects counted as fines (BSE interaction depth)
selected-reference reference not imaged at the same pixel size

known_failure_modes: segmentation threshold drifts with magnification
beam drift or charging at high magnification

redundant_with.increment: D50 is a median above the floor; this extends the distribution below it

provenance.basis: rim scale:M2060 and the ZOOM action rationale in epistemic-field/1

markers.name: High-Z phase elemental identity
markers.observable: Whether the excess fines share the selected-reference additive's elemental identity.
markers.scientific_question: Are the M2060 fines selected-reference additive, another phase, or a mixed interaction-volume signal?
markers.proposition: Which elements make up the excess fine high-Z objects in M2060, compared with the selected-reference additive.
markers.scientific_definition: Elemental composition of the BSE-bright phase per object class (fine vs coarse), relative to the selected-reference additive.
markers.measurement_definition: Paired elemental spectra or maps on M2060 fines and on selected-reference additive particles; element ratios per object class.
markers.capture_requirements: Elemental spectroscopy co-registered with the BSE fields.

existing_data_test.note: BSE grey level depends on mean atomic number and depth; it cannot identify elements.

markers.why_relevant: Supplier attribution of the surviving deviation needs chemistry; the field records composition as not acquired and consequential for M2060.

known_confounds.label: spectroscopy signal volume larger than sub-micrometre fines (mixing with the matrix)

known_failure_modes: fines smaller than the spectral spatial resolution at the chosen kV

provenance.basis: dimension composition (kind missing, would_require) and rim composition:M2060

markers.name: Open-edge deviation phenotype
markers.observable: Whether a measured deviation closes inside the registered section or remains open at a captured edge.
markers.scientific_question: Is the observed shift a bounded local feature or part of a larger spatial zone?
markers.proposition: Classifies each registered deviation as bounded, open at the start, open at the end, or open at both edges.
markers.scientific_definition: A structural phenotype of a spatial KPI profile based on whether it returns to the selected-reference local band before each captured edge.
markers.measurement_definition: Evaluate registered 100 µm local-window means against the descriptive parent-bootstrap reference envelope; record start/end persistence and captured extent without inventing distance beyond the image.
markers.why_relevant: The same scalar deviation can imply a bounded inclusion or an extended zone; the engine already uses the open edge to justify EXTEND without claiming unseen geometry.

known_confounds.label: the selected-reference local band is an approximate analysis support

known_failure_modes: short profiles can leave both boundaries unresolved
registration gaps cannot be interpreted as physical distance

provenance.basis: spatial profile open_at_start/open_at_end and EXTEND action triggers in epistemic-field/1

markers.name: Spatial correlation length
markers.observable: The distance over which porosity or additive-density structure remains spatially correlated.
markers.scientific_question: How far apart must fields be to sample approximately independent structure, and is the present capture long enough?
markers.proposition: Measures the characteristic spatial range of each supported KPI rather than treating adjacent fields as independent replicates.
markers.scientific_definition: The lag at which the registered semivariogram reaches its plateau, or a lower bound when no plateau is observed within the coherent capture.
markers.measurement_definition: Estimate per-KPI semivariograms from registered 25 µm columns, report range only when a plateau is supported, and otherwise report the longest tested lag as a lower bound.
markers.why_relevant: The loaded field shows field-scale porosity structure, while cross-reference comparison changes several morphology interpretations; a parent-aware range can test whether scale explains those regime differences.

known_confounds.label: a range longer than the mosaic cannot be estimated as a closed value

known_failure_modes: a finite mosaic can only lower-bound long-range structure

provenance.basis: implemented spatial_support variograms and SPACE/EXTEND actions in epistemic-field/1

markers.name: Phase-conditioned fines distribution
markers.observable: Fine-particle size and density separated by elemental phase identity rather than BSE brightness alone.
markers.scientific_question: Does the excess persist within the selected-reference additive chemistry, or belong to another phase?
markers.proposition: Conditions the M2060 fine-object distribution on elemental identity so size and composition are not conflated.
markers.scientific_definition: Per-phase number-size distribution of fine objects, with phase identity defined by co-registered elemental spectra or maps.
markers.measurement_definition: Co-register EDS with higher-resolution BSE; assign fine objects to elemental classes; compare per-class size distributions and densities with selected-reference material.
markers.capture_requirements: Co-registered higher-resolution BSE and EDS on M2060 and selected-reference additive particles.

existing_data_test.note: Current BSE intensity cannot assign elemental phase identity.

markers.why_relevant: The decision-driving fines are also at the dim end of the selected-reference BSE range; size and phase identity must be separated before attributing the population.

known_confounds.label: matrix signal can mix into spectra from sub-micrometre fines

known_failure_modes: elemental classes unresolved at the chosen interaction volume

redundant_with.increment: adds elemental phase conditioning to the size distribution

provenance.basis: joint scale and composition limits on the same M2060 fine-object population

markers.name: Scale-dependent phase-fraction heterogeneity
markers.observable: Raw and p(1−p)-normalised fluctuation of porosity or high-Z area fraction as physical window size increases.
markers.scientific_question: Does a phase remain spatially heterogeneous after separating arrangement from the trivial effect of its global fraction?
markers.proposition: The scale curve of local phase-fraction fluctuation can reveal persistent spatial organization that a global phase fraction omits.
markers.scientific_definition: Variance of equal-area local phase fractions over 2–32 µm square windows, reported both raw and divided by p(1−p) when the global fraction is away from zero and one.
markers.measurement_definition: Compute non-overlapping square-window phase fractions at each valid physical scale; retain raw variance, normalized fluctuation, windows, fields and independent parents; compare current, degrees-of-freedom pooled and parent-equal estimates.

existing_data_test.note: The engine now emits the descriptor; scientific discrimination and perturbation robustness remain open.

markers.why_relevant: It treats scale-dependent variance as a candidate marker while preserving the production porosity and area-fraction markers.

known_confounds.label: phase masks and their scale curves can shift with segmentation

known_failure_modes: large windows have few repeats
normalisation is unstable when p is near zero or one

redundant_with.increment: retains raw variance, adds p(1−p) normalisation and parent-aware support audit

markers.name: Scale-dependent particle count overdispersion
markers.observable: How high-Z particle count variance and Fano ratio change with equal-area observation windows.
markers.scientific_question: Are high-Z object counts clustered, Poisson-like, or inhibited across the observed scales?
markers.proposition: The scale curve of number variance relative to mean count can expose spatial organization hidden by mean particle density.
markers.scientific_definition: Number variance and Fano ratio variance(N)/E(N) for centroid counts in equal-area square windows over 2–32 µm scales.
markers.measurement_definition: Count detected high-Z centroids in non-overlapping equal-area windows; retain mean count, number variance, Fano, physical area and support. Treat Poisson only as a comparator, not a diagnosis.

existing_data_test.note: The engine now emits the descriptor; decision value and perturbation robustness remain untested.

markers.why_relevant: Particle density is a count process; its unusual Batch_3 signal remains unusual across eligible frames, so the scale curve can test structural persistence without changing the production density KPI.

known_confounds.label: merged or split objects change both counts and apparent spacing

known_failure_modes: mean counts near zero make Fano unstable
edge and detection-floor effects can mimic overdispersion

redundant_with.increment: adds scale-dependent count variation rather than another mean density

provenance.basis: implemented non-decision descriptor in additive_density spatial support

markers.name: High-Z pair correlation
markers.observable: Excess or deficit of high-Z particle pairs as a function of separation distance.
markers.scientific_question: At which separations does the high-Z phase show clustering or exclusion beyond its mean density?
markers.proposition: An edge-corrected pair-correlation curve can distinguish characteristic spacing from abundance alone.
markers.scientific_definition: Radial pair-correlation function of detected high-Z object centroids, with particle-size and finite-window effects retained as confounds.
markers.measurement_definition: Estimate an edge-corrected pair-correlation curve per parent micrograph and compare parent-level curves over lags supported by every included field.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; no edge-corrected estimator has been validated in this project.

blindspot_refs.label: pair separation and exclusion are not in the production marker vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: It could distinguish equal-density fields with different clustering or exclusion scales.

known_confounds.label: finite fields censor pairs at long separation
finite particle size creates short-range exclusion

known_failure_modes: few particles produce unstable long-lag estimates
uncorrected boundaries bias the curve

redundant_with.increment: a full pair curve can reveal exclusion and preferred spacing before reduction to one range

provenance.basis: point-process and local-fluctuation methods; implementation readiness unclaimed

markers.name: High-Z nearest-neighbour spacing
markers.observable: Distribution of edge-corrected distances from each high-Z object to its nearest neighbours.
markers.scientific_question: Do high-Z objects cluster or maintain exclusion distances after accounting for finite particle size?
markers.proposition: Nearest-neighbour spacing provides an interpretable local companion to the multiscale count curve.
markers.scientific_definition: Distribution of first and selected higher-order centroid-neighbour distances, conditioned on particle size and section geometry.
markers.measurement_definition: Compute edge-corrected neighbour distances per parent and compare the empirical distributions with size-matched selected-reference parents; do not use an unconstrained Poisson null for finite particles.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; 2-D section and finite-particle nulls need explicit validation.

blindspot_refs.label: pair separation and exclusion are not in the production marker vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: It can expose local clustering or regular spacing without replacing particle density.

known_confounds.label: 2-D section distances differ from a true 2-D point process and from 3-D spacing
hard-particle exclusion changes the null spacing

known_failure_modes: boundary particles are censored
merged particles create artificially large distances

redundant_with.increment: more local and interpretable, but less complete across separation scales

provenance.basis: micrograph-derived nearest-neighbour methods; implementation readiness unclaimed

markers.name: Phase-boundary roughness and curvature
markers.observable: Boundary length, curvature and roughness of segmented pores or high-Z regions at a stated physical scale.
markers.scientific_question: Do equal-area phases differ in boundary complexity or interfacial morphology?
markers.proposition: Scale-qualified boundary geometry can reveal morphology that phase fraction alone cannot express.
markers.scientific_definition: Perimeter density and curvature distribution of a segmented phase boundary after a declared, physically scaled boundary estimator.
markers.measurement_definition: Compute boundary descriptors per field at native resolution and under registered segmentation perturbations; aggregate by parent with block support.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; the descriptor is resolution-sensitive and has not been robustified.

blindspot_refs.label: phase-boundary complexity is not in the production marker vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: Area fraction can stay constant while interfacial shape changes materially.

known_confounds.label: perimeter and curvature depend strongly on pixel size and estimator
threshold shifts move the boundary

known_failure_modes: sub-resolution roughness is not observable
raw pixel-chain perimeter is biased

provenance.basis: morphometric image-analysis methods; implementation readiness unclaimed

markers.name: Full phase chord-length distribution
markers.observable: The full distribution of continuous intercept lengths through pore, matrix or high-Z phase.
markers.scientific_question: Do characteristic continuous phase lengths differ even when average chord length or phase fraction does not?
markers.proposition: A parent-level chord distribution retains tail and multimodal structure discarded by the current mean solid-chord marker.
markers.scientific_definition: Empirical distribution of contiguous phase intercept lengths along declared image directions at physical resolution.
markers.measurement_definition: Measure horizontal and, where justified, vertical phase chords per field; preserve direction; compare parent-level empirical distributions with clustered resampling.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; the engine currently retains a mean chord marker, not the full distribution.

blindspot_refs.label: full continuous phase-length distributions are absent from the production vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: The current mean chord length can hide long tails or mixed structural populations.

known_confounds.label: chord distributions are direction-dependent in anisotropic material

known_failure_modes: image edges right-censor long chords
one direction can miss anisotropy

redundant_with.increment: retains the full distribution and explicit directional censoring

provenance.basis: porous-media reconstruction studies show chord distributions contain structure omitted by porosity and two-point summaries

markers.name: Phase lineal-path probability
markers.observable: Probability that a line segment of stated length lies wholly inside one segmented phase.
markers.scientific_question: Does a phase form continuous paths across length scales in the observed 2-D section?
markers.proposition: A lineal-path curve can describe within-section continuity beyond area fraction and two-point co-occurrence.
markers.scientific_definition: Directional lineal-path probability L(r) for the pore or solid indicator field over supported segment lengths.
markers.measurement_definition: Estimate directional L(r) per parent over lengths fully supported by the image; compare curves with parent and spatial-block resampling.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; continuity is restricted to the observed 2-D section.

blindspot_refs.label: full continuous phase-length distributions are absent from the production vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: It offers a continuity-sensitive complement to fraction and chord summaries without claiming 3-D connectivity.

known_confounds.label: 2-D lineal paths do not establish 3-D connectivity

known_failure_modes: long segments are weakly supported
direction pooling can hide anisotropy

redundant_with.increment: expresses survival of whole segments as a scale curve

provenance.basis: standard random-media descriptor; no implementation or decision-readiness claim

markers.name: 2-D Minkowski phase morphology
markers.observable: Area, boundary length and Euler characteristic of each segmented phase at a declared scale.
markers.scientific_question: Do phase amount, interface extent and within-section topology diverge across batches?
markers.proposition: A compact morphology vector can distinguish binary structures with similar phase fraction but different boundary and component topology.
markers.scientific_definition: The 2-D intrinsic-volume vector: phase area, perimeter and Euler characteristic, optionally traced across morphological filter scale.
markers.measurement_definition: Compute the vector per field under native and perturbed segmentations; aggregate at parent level and retain each component rather than collapsing to a score.

existing_data_test.note: Candidate only; scale, digitisation and segmentation stability must be established first.

blindspot_refs.label: within-section phase topology is not in the production marker vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: It exposes perimeter and Euler structure while preserving phase area as a separately auditable component.

known_confounds.label: small components and Euler characteristic are resolution-sensitive
topology can change under small threshold perturbations

known_failure_modes: 2-D Euler characteristic does not establish 3-D connectivity
sub-resolution components destabilize topology

redundant_with.increment: adds perimeter and Euler structure while retaining area explicitly

provenance.basis: Minkowski-function image analysis with explicit resolution caveats; implementation readiness unclaimed

markers.name: Multiscale heterogeneity scaling
markers.observable: How local phase-fraction variability changes with observation window size.
markers.scientific_question: Does spatial scaling discriminate micrographs beyond existing phase-fraction KPIs?
markers.proposition: How the variability of local porosity and additive fraction decays with window size: clustered versus random arrangement.
markers.scientific_definition: Scaling exponent of the coefficient of variation of local phase fraction against window size; a slower decay than a random arrangement indicates clustering.
markers.measurement_definition: CV of local porosity and additive area fraction in windows of 1–16 µm per micrograph; log-log slope; between-micrograph ICC.

blindspot_refs.label: particle and pore arrangement (clustering) is not in the KPI vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: Would add arrangement, not amount, to the vocabulary.

known_confounds.label: phase fractions depend on the segmentation threshold

markers.name: Latent progression axis (pseudotime)
markers.observable: A continuous image-embedding axis that would order material states if robust.
markers.scientific_question: Is there a stable process progression that discrete KPIs miss?
markers.proposition: A learned image embedding orders micrographs along a continuous process-progression axis.
markers.scientific_definition: Leading axis of a self-supervised image embedding (DINOv2 ViT-B/14) of micrograph crops, read as a progression of material state.
markers.measurement_definition: 1875 crops per channel, three normalisations, PCA and diffusion map; stability by leave-one-out, bootstrap and cross-channel agreement.

blindspot_refs.label: continuous process drift between lots is not in the KPI vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: Would expose gradual process drift that discrete KPIs miss.

known_confounds.label: detector black level and contrast stretch differ per micrograph
focus and blur

markers.name: 3-D pore network connectivity
markers.observable: Connected pore volume and path tortuosity through the electrode thickness.
markers.scientific_question: Does the observed 2-D pore morphology form a connected 3-D transport network?
markers.proposition: Connectivity and tortuosity of the pore network, which 2-D cross-sections cannot establish.
markers.scientific_definition: Fraction of pore volume connected across the electrode thickness, and the geometric tortuosity of the connected network.
markers.measurement_definition: Segmented 3-D volume of the electrode; connected-component analysis and path-length tortuosity.

blindspot_refs.label: 3-D transport-relevant pore structure is outside the 2-D section vocabulary

markers.why_relevant: Not tied to the current QC decision: exploratory.

provenance.basis: docs/CLAIMS.md (no tortuosity or 3-D claims from 2-D sections)

capabilities.name: Composition-sensitive mapping (EDS)
capabilities.why_current_workflow_cannot_resolve: BSE contrast cannot distinguish a finer specified additive from a different lower-Z phase; no further BSE capture resolves chemistry.

existing_capability_substitutes.label: BSE grey level of the fines (mean-Z contrast)
existing_capability_substitutes.note: the fines sit at the dim end of the selected-reference range: consistent with a finer additive or with a lower-Z phase

existing_capability_substitutes.label: low-kV, higher-magnification BSE (controller ZOOM)
existing_capability_substitutes.note: may separate sub-surface signal from a lower-Z phase; cannot establish elemental identity. Not yet assessed.

integration.workflow_effect: one extra modality pass on flagged micrographs only
data_interface_requirements: per-object element ratios keyed to engine object classes
composition becomes an acquired dimension in epistemic-field/1

provenance.basis: dimension composition would_require EDS; EDS action rationale and cost class in epistemic-field/1

capabilities.name: 3-D tomography (FIB-SEM or X-ray CT)
capabilities.why_current_workflow_cannot_resolve: Cross-sections are 2-D; connectivity and tortuosity are 3-D properties.

existing_capability_substitutes.label: more independent 2-D sections (controller SECTIONS)
existing_capability_substitutes.note: constrains lot prevalence, not 3-D connectivity. Not yet assessed.

papers.title: Hyperuniformity, quasi-long-range correlations, and void-space constraints in maximally random jammed particle packings. I. Polydisperse spheres

assessments.claim: Local volume-fraction variance across observation-window size is a meaningful scale-dependent descriptor distinct from point-number fluctuation.
assessments.note: Supports the descriptor family, not a battery-electrode decision threshold.

assessments.claim: Local number variance is a scale-dependent point-process statistic and differs conceptually from local volume-fraction fluctuation.
assessments.note: Supports number variance; the simple Fano comparator remains a project choice.

assessments.claim: Pair correlation describes average neighbours around a reference point and contributes to local number fluctuation.
assessments.note: Supports investigating a full separation-dependent point-process descriptor.

papers.title: Nth-nearest neighbor statistics for analysis of particle distribution data derived from micrographs

assessments.claim: Micrograph-derived nearest-neighbour statistics can characterize particle clustering, but the reference must respect finite-particle inhibition and section geometry.
assessments.note: Directly motivates both the candidate and its stated confounds.

papers.title: Structural and Transport Properties of Alumina Porous Membranes from Process-Based and Statistical Reconstruction Techniques
papers.venue: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science

assessments.claim: Pore and solid chord-length distributions can retain structural information that porosity and two-point correlation alone do not.
assessments.note: Supports preserving the full distribution rather than another mean.

assessments.claim: Matching a two-point correlation alone was insufficient to reproduce all structural and transport behaviour in the studied porous membranes.
assessments.note: A scope limit: pair correlation should remain one candidate among complementary descriptors.

papers.title: Quantification of soil structure based on Minkowski functions

assessments.claim: Minkowski functions provide compact phase volume, interface and topology descriptors, with explicit resolution dependence.
assessments.note: Supports a cautious 2-D candidate and its resolution caveat.

assessments.claim: Interface measures can add structural information beyond phase volume, but resolution controls quantitative reliability.
assessments.note: Indirect support for boundary-length investigation; curvature needs separate evidence.

records.title: Scale rim: the excess high-Z population piles up at the detection floor

assessments.claim: The population is truncated by the current pixel size: not computable from existing micrographs, observable with a finer BSE pixel.

records.title: Composition rim: BSE alone cannot identify the deviating phase

assessments.claim: BSE alone cannot separate a finer additive from a different lower-Z phase.
A phase-conditioned size distribution requires elemental identity that the current BSE capture does not contain.

records.title: Registered profile: M2060 remains outside the local band at the captured start

assessments.claim: The registered profile supports a bounded/open-edge categorical state from current data without extrapolating beyond the image.
The edge state adds spatial extent information beyond the micrograph-level scalar deviation.
The open start is the structured trigger for extending the M2060 mosaic.

records.title: Spatial support: additive-density range exceeds the coherent reference capture

assessments.claim: The current registered fields support a variogram and a lower bound on additive-density correlation length.
Correlation range adds field-spacing and capture-extent information not present in mean additive density.

records.title: Spatial support: porosity correlation range is approximately 175 µm

assessments.claim: The current registered fields support an approximately 175 µm porosity correlation range.

records.title: Spatial support: raw and normalized phase-fraction heterogeneity curves

assessments.claim: Existing segmentations support raw and p(1−p)-normalised phase-fraction variance at each valid 2–32 µm scale with explicit window and parent counts.
The new curve is more auditable than the rejected earlier scaling exponent, but incremental scientific discrimination has not yet been shown.

records.title: Spatial support: high-Z number variance and Fano curves

assessments.claim: Existing centroid maps support count mean, number variance and Fano descriptors in equally supported 2–32 µm windows with explicit parent counts.
Count overdispersion describes arrangement relative to count intensity and is not another estimate of mean particle density.

records.title: Research log #4: acquisition differs per micrograph

assessments.claim: The embedding was computed from existing crops of every micrograph.
The leading axis tracks black level (ρ≈0.8) and disagrees across detectors and normalisations (|ρ| 0.07–0.25); a 1.5 px blur moves a tile about as far as the gap between micrographs.

records.title: Research log #6: no progression in robust KPIs

assessments.claim: Micrograph-level robust KPIs show no coherent dominant axis: discrete micrograph offsets, not a continuum.
Computed from existing segmentations for every micrograph: exponents −0.5…−0.7 (clustered, not random).
Between-micrograph ICC 0.2–0.3: a property of the material class, not discriminating between micrographs.

records.title: Research log #11: M2060 has an excess of fine high-Z objects

assessments.claim: The excess drives the Batch 3 REJECT; its chemistry, or a sub-surface fraction, is uncertain (fines at the dim end of the selected-reference BSE range).
Conditioning the fine-object distribution on phase identity would discriminate selected-reference additive fines from another lower-Z phase.

records.title: Claims: no 3-D or tortuosity claims from 2-D sections

source.locator: 3-D particle sizes, absolute porosity or tortuosity

assessments.claim: The dataset is 2-D sections of non-infiltrated pores; connectivity and tortuosity cannot be measured from it.
